tldr: DSPy replaces hand-written prompt strings with typed signatures, parameterized modules, and teleprompters that compile a pipeline against a metric, bootstrapping demonstrations so GPT-3.5 and llama2-13b-chat self-improve GSM8K and HotPotQA programs without prompt engineering.
method: A program declares Signatures: typed input/output fields like "question -> answer", not prompt strings. Modules wrap a signature — Predict formats signature plus demonstrations into a prompt, calls the LM, parses output fields, and in compile mode records input/output traces. ChainOfThought merely prepends a rationale output field and delegates to Predict; ReAct, ProgramOfThought and MultiChainComparison are likewise built from Predict. Modules compose in a define-by-run forward() method (retrieve, then answer). A teleprompter compiles the program given a trainset plus metric in three stages: (1) candidate generation — recursively find unique Predict modules, simulate the program, and keep multi-stage traces whose final output passes the metric as demonstrations for each signature; (2) parameter optimization — select demonstration sets by random search or Optuna, or update LM weights via BootstrapFinetune; (3) higher-order optimization — ensemble the top bootstrapped programs by majority voting. What evolves is demonstrations and field instructions, not weights, unless finetuning.
results: GSM8K, GPT-3.5 dev/test: vanilla zero-shot 24.0 → bootstrap×2 64.7/61.7; CoT 50.0 → bootstrap 80.3/72.9 → +ensemble 88.3/81.6, matching the 8-shot fewshot+human-CoT baseline (78.6/72.4); reflection (5 sampled chains compared by MultiChainComparison) 83.0/76.0 and 86.7 dev ensembled. The paper's summary: composing modules instead of strings lifts LMs from 4-20% to 49-88% accuracy.

GSM8K, llama2-13b-chat dev/test: vanilla 7.0/9.4 → bootstrap×2 37.3/36.5; CoT 26.7 → bootstrap 43.3 (+ensemble 43.7 dev) vs 34.3 with human CoT demonstrations; reflection 36.7 → 44.3 bootstrap / 49.0 ensembled, 40.2/46.9 test.

HotPotQA answer EM, GPT-3.5 dev/test: CoT RAG fewshot 36.4 → bootstrap 42.3; multihop (two-hop query generation) 36.9 → 48.7 bootstrap (47.0 passage accuracy) → 54.7 ensemble dev, 31.2 → 39.6 → 45.6 test (ensemble scored on 50% of test due to cost). llama2-13b-chat multihop: 34.7 → 42.0 → 50.0 dev, 31.3 → 36.4 → 41.0 test.
HotPotQA ReAct dev EM: GPT-3.5 zero-shot 20.3, +human reasoning 33.0, bootstrap 31.0, bootstrap×2 39.0; llama2-13b-chat 20.0, 28.3, 24.7, 40.0 — bootstrap×2 beats the expert-written ReAct traces.

BootstrapFinetune distils a multihop program into T5-Large (770M): 39.3% answer EM and 46.0% passage accuracy on dev, from 200 labeled inputs plus 800 unlabeled questions and a teacher that is an ensemble of two llama2-13b-chat multihop programs.
advantages: Prompt strings stop being the interface: the same two-to-four-module programs and the same compilers run on GPT-3.5 and llama2-13b-chat, and bootstrapped demonstrations match or beat expert-written ones (GSM8K CoT 80.3 vs 78.6 dev with human CoT; llama2-13b-chat CoT 43.3 vs 34.3).

Label-efficiency by construction: only final-output labels are assumed, while intermediate reasoning chains and retrieval contexts are bootstrapped, so a new pipeline is recompiled rather than re-annotated with step-specific data.

Compiling closes the LM gap — llama2-13b-chat multihop at 42.0 dev EM vs GPT-3.5 fewshot at 36.9 — and BootstrapFinetune pushes the pipeline into a 770M T5, which the paper argues means orders-of-magnitude cheaper inference than a proprietary LM.

One optimizer abstraction covers prompting and finetuning, and a teacher program can be composed in (an expensive large-LM ensemble supervises a cheap student), which is what makes the T5 result possible.
limitations: A well-defined automatic metric plus at least a few training inputs the LM can actually pass are prerequisites; bootstrapping works by rejection-sampling traces that satisfy the metric, so a program (or LM) that never passes yields no demonstrations.
The empirical evidence is two case studies, GSM8K and HotPotQA; the conclusion explicitly defers other tasks (information extraction, low-resource synthetic data generation) to future work.

Compiling is not free: minutes to tens of minutes and thousands of program runs (10-20 trials over 150-300 validation examples), and it was costly enough that the HotPotQA ensemble test number is marked as evaluated on 50% of the test set.

The optimizer scope in this version is narrow: "In this iteration of DSPy, we focus on demonstrations", Stage 3 control-flow optimization is only ensembling (dynamic test-time bootstrapping and backtracking are future work), and optional field data types are "not core to DSPy at the time of writing".
fits: Stage 2 (optimization-as-language): the substrate that turns prompt optimization into whole-pipeline compilation, and the direct ancestor of the harness-level optimizers in stages 4-6. Pairs with OPRO (2309.03409) and APE as the single-prompt optimizers it generalizes, and with Reflexion (2303.11366) for the feedback signal; its teleprompter/optimizer split recurs in later harness cards.
reading: Read §3 (signatures, modules, teleprompters) and §4 (the three compiler stages) first — that is the mechanism. Then §6 with Table 1 and §7 with Table 2 for the numbers, and Appendix E for BootstrapFewShot pseudocode.
